lastCompletedStory.title: Route result.ts worker-report sites through parseWorkerReport and delete WorkerReportFallback

openQuestions: US-003's AC1 oracle ([oracle: file-assert grep -Lq 'WorkerReportFallback' src/supervisor/result.ts]) is expected to report FAIL when the reviewer (Layer B) re-runs it verbatim, even though WorkerReportFallback is genuinely deleted from result.ts (confirmed via grep -c and manual read, and via typecheck/bun test all green). Root cause: BSD/macOS grep's -q flag nullifies -L's exit-status inversion, so grep -Lq PATTERN FILE exits 1 whenever PATTERN is absent and 0 only when PATTERN is present -- the literal opposite of what a negative-existence file-assert oracle intends. Verified empirically via runBehavioralGate in a real tmux session, not just the interactive-shell grep wrapper. This is a PRD-authoring defect in the oracle's chosen grep flags (would need `! grep -q PATTERN FILE` instead to invert correctly on both GNU and BSD grep), not an implementation defect -- do not 'fix' it by reintroducing WorkerReportFallback. Documented in scripts/cam/patterns.md for the reviewer/planner.
nextStoryContext: result.ts now delegates its worker-report read path entirely to the shared report-parse.ts parser: tryReadWorkerReport(reportPath, readFile) calls parseWorkerReport(text) and returns WorkerReport | null (the canonical type from worker-report.ts, imported via report-parse.ts's re-export). The old local WorkerReportFallback interface is gone. extractRecordedTestsGate(report: WorkerReport) is now a one-liner (report.gates?.tests) since parseWorkerReport already fail-closes a malformed gates field at parse time (a present-but-invalid gates rejects the WHOLE report to null before extractRecordedTestsGate ever sees it) -- there is no remaining need for the old isObject(gates) + typeof tests==='string' runtime guard inside extractRecordedTestsGate itself. The inline re-check `typeof report.outcome === 'string' && typeof report.story === 'string'` in the PRIMARY path of readWorkerOutcome was replaced by a plain `if (report)` truthiness check, since parseWorkerReport already guarantees both fields are strings when it returns non-null. No other call sites in the codebase referenced WorkerReportFallback (grep-verified). This completes the report-parse.ts wiring arc across all three consumers: host.ts + loop.ts (US-002) and result.ts (US-003, this story) all now share ONE parser contract -- if a future story adds a fourth worker-report reader, it should follow this same pattern (call parseWorkerReport(rawText) directly if the input is already raw text; round-trip via JSON.stringify per the US-002 patterns.md bullet if the input is already a statically-typed-but-not-runtime-guaranteed object).

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure internal refactor wiring result.ts onto the shared report-parse.ts parser (from US-001, already validated in that story); no external library surface touched.
